renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: qv_vs_completeness
  title: Consensus QV against k-mer completeness
  description: |-
    Each point is an assembly: the share of solid read k-mers it recovers on the horizontal axis and its consensus quality value (QV) on the vertical axis, sized by its number of k-mers. It answers which assemblies are both complete and accurate.
    How to read: the best assemblies sit top right. High completeness with a low QV is an assembly that kept everything but was not polished; high QV with low completeness is an accurate assembly that lost sequence. Open the copy-number tile to see whether the lost k-mers are absent or only duplicated.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median consensus QV of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Merqury. QV is the Phred-scaled error rate (QV 40 is one error per 10 kb), so compare assemblies of the same project with each other.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/marbl/merqury/2.-Overall-k-mer-evaluation.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32928274/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: K-mer completeness (%)
    y_title: Consensus QV
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: kmer_completeness
    y: qv
    label: assembly_id
    color: assembly_id
    size: total_kmers

- component: figure
  title: Consensus QV per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly and its height is the consensus QV Merqury derives from k-mers found in the assembly but not in the reads. The bar colour is the k-mer completeness, so one tile shows accuracy and completeness together.
    How to read: taller bars are more accurate. A tall pale bar is accurate but incomplete, a short dark bar complete but error-prone; polish the second and investigate the first.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median consensus QV of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Merqury.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/marbl/merqury/2.-Overall-k-mer-evaluation.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembly_id
    y: qv
    color: kmer_completeness
    labels:
      assembly_id: Assembly
      qv: Consensus QV
      kmer_completeness: K-mer completeness (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: qv

- component: card
  title: Best consensus QV
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest consensus QV over the assemblies in view and the box shows how the assemblies spread. It answers how accurate the best assembly is and how far the others sit from it.
    How to read: a wide box means the assemblies differ a lot in polish, so compare them in the scatter above before choosing one. QV is logarithmic, so every 10 points is a tenfold lower error rate.
  column: qv
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: QV, quartiles over assemblies
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Median k-mer completeness
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of solid read k-mers found in the assemblies, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much of the sequenced genome the assemblies kept.
    How to read: values near 100 mean almost nothing was lost. A low box means missing sequence, so check the copy-number composition for the absent share.
  column: kmer_completeness
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: completeness, quartiles over assemblies

- component: card
  title: Error k-mers in the worst assembly
  description: |-
    Error k-mers are k-mers present in the assembly and absent from the reads, so each marks a probable base error. The hero number is the largest count over the assemblies and the histogram shows their distribution.
    How to read: a count that stands far above the median points to one assembly in need of polishing. Counts depend on assembly size, so read them next to the QV.
  column: asm_only_kmers
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: error k-mers, distribution over assemblies

- component: table
  title: Assembly quality table
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly with its error k-mers, total k-mers, QV, error rate and the solid k-mers shared with the reads. It answers the exact numbers behind the scatter and the cards.
    How to read: sort by QV or completeness to rank the assemblies, and compare the solid k-mers of the assembly and of the reads to see what was lost.

outputs.name: Read k-mer copy number in the assembly

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: copy_number_bars
  title: Read k-mer copy number per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly, split by how many times its solid read k-mers occur in it: absent, once, twice and so on. It answers how much sequence the assembly lost and how much it duplicated.
    How to read: on a haploid or collapsed assembly nearly all k-mers should be present once. A large absent share is lost sequence and a large two-copy share is duplicated sequence such as retained haplotigs.
    Note: read k-mers at or below the error trough of the read spectrum are left out, so sequencing errors do not count as absent sequence.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marbl/merqury/master/README.md
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Share of solid read k-mers (%)
  roles:
    sample_id: assembly_id
    taxon: copy_class
    rank: rank
    abundance: percent

- component: figure
  title: Copy number shares, stacked
  description: |-
    Each stacked bar is an assembly and each segment the share of its solid read k-mers at one copy number. It answers the same question as the advanced tile above in a fixed, printable form.
    How to read: compare the single-copy segment across assemblies; the larger it is, the more faithful the assembly is to the reads.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assembly_id
    y: percent
    color: copy_class
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      assembly_id: Assembly
      percent: Share of solid read k-mers (%)
      copy_class: Copies in the assembly

- component: card
  title: Single-copy k-mer share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of solid read k-mers present exactly once in an assembly, the signature of a clean haploid or collapsed assembly. The histogram shows how the assemblies spread.
    How to read: values near 100 are expected for a haploid assembly. A low value means missing or duplicated sequence, so open the stacked bars to see which. A diploid or polyploid assembly legitimately holds more copies.
  column: percent
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  filter_expr: col('copy_class') == '1 copy'
  caption: single-copy share, distribution over assemblies
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: K-mers by copy number
  description: |-
    Each unit is a solid read k-mer and the ring splits them by how often the assembly holds them. It answers how the k-mers of all assemblies in view are distributed over the copy classes.
    How to read: one dominant single-copy slice is healthy. Large absent or multi-copy slices mean lost or duplicated sequence.
  column: solid_kmers
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: copy_class
  caption: solid read k-mers, by copy number

- component: table
  title: Copy number table
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly and a copy class with its solid k-mer count and share. It answers the exact numbers behind the stacked bars.
    How to read: sort by share to find the assemblies with the largest absent or two-copy class.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: sequence_qv_scatter
  title: Sequence QV against size
  description: |-
    Each point is a contig or scaffold: its number of k-mers, a proxy for its length, against its consensus QV. It answers which sequences carry the lowest accuracy and whether they are small or large.
    How to read: errors are rarely even, so a few short low-QV sequences often hold most error k-mers. The lowest points are labelled; inspect, polish or drop them. A low QV on a large sequence matters more than on a short one.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median consensus QV of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Merqury. The horizontal axis is logarithmic.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/marbl/merqury/2.-Overall-k-mer-evaluation.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: K-mers in the sequence (size)
    y_title: Consensus QV
    log_x: true
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 8
    label_order_col: qv
  roles:
    x: total_kmers
    y: qv
    label: sequence
    color: assembly_id

- component: figure
  title: Per-sequence QV distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts sequences in a QV bin, one overlaid histogram per assembly. It answers how uniform the accuracy of an assembly is.
    How to read: a narrow histogram at high QV is an evenly accurate assembly. A long tail to the left is a set of weak sequences, so open the scatter to see which. Histograms of different assemblies are overlaid, not stacked.
    Note: sequences with no error k-mer have no finite QV and are not drawn.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median consensus QV of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Merqury.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: qv
    color: assembly_id
    barmode: overlay
    opacity: 0.6
    labels:
      qv: Consensus QV
      assembly_id: Assembly
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: qv

- component: card
  title: Lowest sequence QV
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest QV over all sequences in view and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how bad the worst sequence is compared with a typical one.
    How to read: a minimum far below the median marks a sequence worth inspecting. QV is logarithmic, so a few points of difference are a large error ratio.
  column: qv
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: QV, distribution over sequences

- component: card
  title: Sequences with no error k-mer
  description: |-
    The hero number is the number of assemblies and the second figure the number of sequences; the ring splits the sequences into those with and without any error k-mer. It answers how many sequences are perfectly supported by the reads.
    How to read: error-free sequences are mostly short, so a large error-free share alone is not proof of a good assembly. Read it next to the QV of the large sequences.
  column: assembly_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: error_free
  caption: sequences, by error-free status

- component: card
  title: Error k-mers per sequence
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest count of error k-mers on a single sequence, with the median and the total beside it. It answers whether the errors are concentrated on a few sequences.
    How to read: a maximum far above the median means a handful of sequences carry most errors and polishing them gives the biggest gain.
  column: asm_only_kmers
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - sum
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: error k-mers, distribution over sequences

- component: table
  title: Sequence QV table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequence of an assembly with its error k-mers, total k-mers, QV and error rate. It answers which named sequences to inspect.
    How to read: sort by QV ascending to list the weakest sequences first, and by error k-mers to find where most errors sit.
